How it works

  1. You post or call. Boat, engine make and model, hours if you know them, what it's doing, where it sits, photos if you have them.
  2. A human calls you back. Within 5 minutes during the day. We confirm the details and make sure it's a job we can help with.
  3. We offer it to the best-matched mechanics. Two or three insured independents near you who work on your engine brand. The first to accept gets it, and texts you his name and a time window.
  4. Written quote before work. For anything beyond a diagnostic visit, you get a quote by text or email and approve it with one tap. Parts are billed at the final invoiced amount; labor as quoted unless the job changes, in which case you approve first.
  5. Fixed at your dock. You don't need to be there. The mechanic sends photos of the work and the old parts.
  6. Pay when it's done. You get a link showing the itemized invoice. Pay by bank transfer at the invoiced amount, or by card with a small processing fee shown up front. We pay the mechanic.

What the mechanics are vetted on

  • Years of experience and brand certifications
  • Commercial general liability insurance, certificate on file and renewal tracked
  • A signed standards agreement: show up, quote in writing, honor the quote, clean up
  • Customer reviews on every job, visible to our dispatchers

What it costs

You pay the mechanic's price. Mobile marine labor in Tampa Bay runs roughly $120 to $150 an hour, with a trip or diagnostic fee around $75 to $150 that is usually credited toward the repair. Our fee comes out of the mechanic's side, in exchange for sending them work and handling the billing.
